pr_body:
# Objective

- Fix https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/11453.
- Fix https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/7332.

## Solution

I created a `plugin_group!` macro that takes in a list of `Plugin`s and then generates a `PluginGroup` along with it's documentation.

---

## Changelog

- Bevy App: Added the `plugin_group!` macro, which allows easy creation of `PluginGroup`s.

issue_context.title: `DefaultPlugins` documentation is out of date
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?

Documentation of [default plugins](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_internal/src/default_plugins.rs#L3-L37) is missing `AccessibilityPlugin`.

Also see #7332

review_comments: This shouldn't be added to documentation.
I agree but I couldn't find a way to exclude this from the documentation via the macro. (macros are hard, suggestions are welcome)
I'm not experienced with macros, but maybe we can make it respect `#[doc(hidden)]`?
Well I would need to check if `#[doc(hidden)]` is present and then hide the documentation entry.
Fixed in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/11460/commits/ab5ff9774d368389d72ef36225ace8129184a80d

I don't think an `ident` works well here. Perhaps it could be a:

- `path`: _TypePath_
- `ty`: _Type_
  - I don't know the difference between a type path and just a type, but it may be worth investigating.
- `expr`: _Expression_
  - Instead of requiring every plugin implement default, you could instead require an expression and manually write `MyPlugin::default()` for each.

There's a list in the [Rust Reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/macros-by-example.html#metavariables) that you can skim through to see what works well here. This would help remove the weird triple-colon `:::` shenanigans going on too.

The reason it looks like this is because I need to get 2 things from the path (for documentation): The short name, and the full path. The full path part is easy, but getting the short name is not. The way I solved this is by seperating the short name from the rest of the path with an additional colon (This is needed due to local ambiguity or whatever).
I'm not really a fan of that syntax, since it doesn't really look like a path.
Ok, that's fine. :)
